interaction.channel: CDP pointer input against both production Browser renderers
steps: Both renderers open the Terminal surface on the canonical seeded thread.
Both renderers receive a visible New Terminal pointer action and expose Terminal 2.
Lynx Terminal 2 writes and renders LYNX_TERM_2_MARKER.
Lynx switches to Terminal 1, writes and renders LYNX_TERM_1_MARKER, then switches back.
Terminal 2 history contains only its marker, proving per-ID history isolation.
Closing active Terminal 2 returns to Terminal 1 and restores its distinct history.

productLossClosed: Lynx is no longer limited to one hard-coded terminal ID.
New, switch, close, active-neighbor fallback, and per-session history isolation now match the Web authority lifecycle at the bounded tab/session level.
harnessLossExcluded: Early runs omitted the new thread-route classification, selected a draft Web route, and were rejected by identity and geometry gates.
The Browser-preview adapter initially rejected the Native-only terminal focus handshake; the adapter now records an explicit no-op instead of emitting renderer errors.
One pristine diagnostic run had a transient VCS status read error and was rejected rather than filtered.
remainingProductResidual: Terminal split groups, xterm key-by-key semantics, selection actions, and physical drag remain outside this bounded slice.
classification.remainingBoundary: Native exact-owned Computer Use correlation is still required before Native cells receive credit.
classification.policy: No state weight, threshold, bad sample filter, or scope reduction was used.
